claim: Kit is a proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase that is evolutionarily conserved and loss-of-function intolerant (pLI = 0.98 and LOEUF of 0.17).
source: The proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase Kit (aliases c-Kit, CD117; human gene symbol KIT, mouse gene symbol Kit) is an evolutionarily conserved, loss-of-function intolerant, gene that is enriched in specific neuron populations and tentatively associated with rare cases of neurological dysfunction (pLI = 0.98 and LOEUF of 0.17) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B; Chen et al., 2022; Bernstein et al., 1990).
evidence: The pLI and LOEUF scores are cited from Chen et al., 2022 and Bernstein et al., 1990, and referenced to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Kit is enriched in specific neuron populations and tentatively associated with rare cases of neurological dysfunction.
source: The proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase Kit (aliases c-Kit, CD117; human gene symbol KIT, mouse gene symbol Kit) is an evolutionarily conserved, loss-of-function intolerant, gene that is enriched in specific neuron populations and tentatively associated with rare cases of neurological dysfunction (pLI = 0.98 and LOEUF of 0.17) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B; Chen et al., 2022; Bernstein et al., 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2022 and Bernstein et al., 1990, and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Kit mutations can result in diverse conditions such as hypo- or hyperpigmentation or melanoma, anemia or leukemia, infertility, mastocytosis, and impaired gut motility or gastrointestinal tumors.
source: Thus, Kit mutations can result in diverse conditions such as hypo- or hyperpigmentation or melanoma, anemia or leukemia, infertility, mastocytosis, and impaired gut motility or gastrointestinal tumors (Kit biology reviewed Bernstein et al., 1990; Lennartsson and Rönnstrand, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to reviews by Bernstein et al., 1990 and Lennartsson and Rönnstrand, 2012.

claim: Kit Ligand (KL) and Kit are mutually expressed in discrete neuron populations known to be connected across several decades and species.
source: Across several decades and species, it has been reported that KL and Kit are mutually expressed in discrete neuron populations known to be connected; it has thus been hypothesized that the expression pattern of KL-Kit may reflect a role in connectivity (Keshet et al., 1991; Motro et al., 1991; Hirota et al., 1992; Manova et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Keshet et al., 1991; Motro et al., 1991; Hirota et al., 1992; Manova et al., 1992.

claim: Inactivating Kit mutations have been implicated with disorders of the central nervous system including developmental delay, ataxia, hypotonia, intellectual disability, deafness, and autism spectrum disorder.
source: Consistent with such a function, case reports have implicated inactivating Kit mutations with disorders of the central nervous system (Telfer et al., 1971; Finucane et al., 1991; Funderburk and Crandall, 1974; Lacassie et al., 1977; Kilsby et al., 2013; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C). Clinical phenotypes include developmental delay, ataxia, hypotonia, intellectual disability, deafness, and autism spectrum disorder.
evidence: This claim is supported by case report citations (Telfer et al., 1971; Finucane et al., 1991; Funderburk and Crandall, 1974; Lacassie et al., 1977; Kilsby et al., 2013) and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: KL or Kit mutation or pharmacological manipulation alters outgrowth of spinal commissural axons in vitro.
source: KL or Kit mutation or pharmacological manipulation alters outgrowth of spinal commissural axons in vitro (Gore et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gore et al., 2008.

claim: KL stimulates cortical neurite outgrowth in vitro.
source: KL stimulates cortical neurite outgrowth in vitro (Su et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Su et al., 2013.

claim: Kit reduction in cortex of developing rats or mice delays axon extension.
source: Kit reduction in cortex of developing rats or mice delays axon extension (Guijarro et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Guijarro et al., 2013.

claim: Severe global KL-Kit hypomorphs exhibit fatal anemia.
source: Functional studies of KL-Kit in synaptic physiology have likely been hampered by pleiotropy and organismal or cell death. Severe global KL-Kit hypomorphs exhibit fatal anemia, and developmental Kit depletion or inhibition in the cerebrum has resulted in the death of neuronal progenitors or nascent neurons (Guijarro et al., 2013; Mashayekhi and Gholizadeh, 2011; Aoki et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Guijarro et al., 2013; Mashayekhi and Gholizadeh, 2011; Aoki et al., 2017.

claim: Developmental Kit depletion or inhibition in the cerebrum has resulted in the death of neuronal progenitors or nascent neurons.
source: Severe global KL-Kit hypomorphs exhibit fatal anemia, and developmental Kit depletion or inhibition in the cerebrum has resulted in the death of neuronal progenitors or nascent neurons (Guijarro et al., 2013; Mashayekhi and Gholizadeh, 2011; Aoki et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Guijarro et al., 2013; Mashayekhi and Gholizadeh, 2011; Aoki et al., 2017.

claim: In mice, rats, and humans, Kit is abundantly expressed by molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) of the cerebellar cortex.
source: In mice, rats, and humans, Kit is abundantly expressed by molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) of the cerebellar cortex (Motro et al., 1991; Hirota et al., 1992; Manova et al., 1992; Kim et al., 2003)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Motro et al., 1991; Hirota et al., 1992; Manova et al., 1992; Kim et al., 2003.

claim: Cerebellar Kit Ligand is restricted to Purkinje cells (PCs).
source: In mice, rats, and humans, Kit is abundantly expressed by molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) of the cerebellar cortex (Motro et al., 1991; Hirota et al., 1992; Manova et al., 1992; Kim et al., 2003), while cerebellar KL is restricted to Purkinje cells (PCs), which MLIs provide GABAergic synaptic inhibition to.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Motro et al., 1991; Hirota et al., 1992; Manova et al., 1992; Kim et al., 2003, and the context of the sentence.

claim: MLIs provide GABAergic synaptic inhibition to Purkinje cells.
source: In mice, rats, and humans, Kit is abundantly expressed by molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) of the cerebellar cortex (Motro et al., 1991; Hirota et al., 1992; Manova et al., 1992; Kim et al., 2003), while cerebellar KL is restricted to Purkinje cells (PCs), which MLIs provide GABAergic synaptic inhibition to.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cerebellar circuitry.

claim: Kit tm1c homozygous Control animals had normal appearance, sex ratios, and reproductive success.
source: Kit tm1c homozygous Control animals had normal appearance, sex ratios, and reproductive success.
evidence: This is an observation reported by the authors about their generated mouse strain.

claim: Kit protein is abundantly expressed in parvalbumin-positive GABAergic interneurons in the molecular layer of the cerebellar cortex (MLIs).
source: Kit protein is abundantly expressed in parvalbumin-positive GABAergic interneurons in the molecular layer of the cerebellar cortex (MLIs), whereas KL is expressed by PCs (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A and B, which shows immunohistochemistry data.

claim: KL is expressed by Purkinje cells.
source: Kit protein is abundantly expressed in parvalbumin-positive GABAergic interneurons in the molecular layer of the cerebellar cortex (MLIs), whereas KL is expressed by PCs (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A and B.

claim: Pax2 is a transcription factor expressed early in the lineage of GABAergic interneurons of the cerebellum.
source: Pax2 is a transcription factor expressed early in the lineage of GABAergic interneurons of the cerebellum (Maricich and Herrup, 1999)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Maricich and Herrup, 1999.

claim: A Pax2-Cre transgene enables embryonic recombination.
source: Pax2 is a transcription factor expressed early in the lineage of GABAergic interneurons of the cerebellum (Maricich and Herrup, 1999); a Pax2-Cre transgene enables embryonic recombination (Blake and Ziman, 2014; Pfeffer et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blake and Ziman, 2014; Pfeffer et al., 2002.

claim: Control and Kit KO animals were produced in normal sex and genotype ratios.
source: We produced Control and Kit KO animals in normal sex and genotype ratios.
evidence: This is an observation reported by the authors.

claim: Control littermates had dark coat and eyes, but littermate Kit KO animals had white whiskers, white fur with variable pigmented patches, and black eyes.
source: As expected for the C57BL/6J background, Control littermates had dark coat and eyes, but littermate Kit KO animals had white whiskers, white fur with variable pigmented patches, and black eyes; example littermates are provided in Figure 1E.
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1E showing example littermates.

claim: Pax2 is expressed in melanocytes.
source: Given Pax2 expression in melanocytes (Lee et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2011.

claim: Kit plays a role in melanogenesis.
source: Given Pax2 expression in melanocytes (Lee et al., 2011) and the role of Kit in melanogenesis reviewed in Wehrle-Haller, 2003; Besmer et al., 1993
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to reviews by Wehrle-Haller, 2003; Besmer et al., 1993.

claim: In Control animals, Kit immunoreactivity is present in the parvalbumin-positive MLIs of the cerebellar cortex.
source: By immunohistochemistry in Control animals, we recapitulated the known pattern of Kit immunoreactivity in the parvalbumin-positive MLIs of the cerebellar cortex (Control, Figure 1F and inset).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1F showing immunohistochemistry data.

claim: In Kit KO animals, cerebellar Kit immunoreactivity is lost.
source: In contrast, a sex-matched Kit KO littermate demonstrated loss of cerebellar Kit immunoreactivity (Kit KO, Figure 1F and inset).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1F showing immunohistochemistry data.

claim: mGlur1/2 and neurogranin-positive cerebellar Golgi cells were still present in the Kit KO condition.
source: In data not shown, we confirmed that both mGlur1/2 and neurogranin-positive cerebellar Golgi cells (which share the MLI Pax2+ lineage, and of which some are transiently Kit positive) were still present in the Kit KO condition (Maricich and Herrup, 1999; Leto et al., 2006; Weisheit et al., 2006; Amat et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' statement and citations to Maricich and Herrup, 1999; Leto et al., 2006; Weisheit et al., 2006; Amat et al., 2017.

claim: Golgi cells share the MLI Pax2+ lineage, and some are transiently Kit positive.
source: In data not shown, we confirmed that both mGlur1/2 and neurogranin-positive cerebellar Golgi cells (which share the MLI Pax2+ lineage, and of which some are transiently Kit positive) were still present in the Kit KO condition (Maricich and Herrup, 1999; Leto et al., 2006; Weisheit et al., 2006; Amat et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Maricich and Herrup, 1999; Leto et al., 2006; Weisheit et al., 2006; Amat et al., 2017.

claim: By western blot of cerebellar lysates from Control animals, Kit resolved as a major band at ~120 kD.
source: By western blot of cerebellar lysates from Control animals, Kit resolved as a major band at ~120 kD, but in Kit KO littermates, Kit immunoreactivity was lost; GAPDH as loading control was equivalent, as was parvalbumin (which marks mature MLIs and PCs) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1G showing western blot data.

claim: In Kit KO littermates, Kit immunoreactivity was lost by western blot.
source: By western blot of cerebellar lysates from Control animals, Kit resolved as a major band at ~120 kD, but in Kit KO littermates, Kit immunoreactivity was lost; GAPDH as loading control was equivalent, as was parvalbumin (which marks mature MLIs and PCs) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1G showing western blot data.

claim: GAPDH and parvalbumin levels were equivalent between Control and Kit KO by western blot.
source: By western blot of cerebellar lysates from Control animals, Kit resolved as a major band at ~120 kD, but in Kit KO littermates, Kit immunoreactivity was lost; GAPDH as loading control was equivalent, as was parvalbumin (which marks mature MLIs and PCs) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1G showing western blot data.

claim: Parvalbumin marks mature MLIs and PCs.
source: By western blot of cerebellar lysates from Control animals, Kit resolved as a major band at ~120 kD, but in Kit KO littermates, Kit immunoreactivity was lost; GAPDH as loading control was equivalent, as was parvalbumin (which marks mature MLIs and PCs) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is established knowledge about parvalbumin expression in the cerebellum.

claim: Kit KO was associated with a significant change in the distribution of sIPSC event amplitudes in PCs.
source: Kit KO was associated with a significant change in the distribution of sIPSC event amplitudes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2C showing frequency distribution data.

claim: Kit KO produced a significant decrease in sIPSC frequency in PCs.
source: We determined there was a significant decrease in sIPSC frequency (Figure 2D)
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2D showing quantification data.

claim: Kit KO produced a less severe decrease of sIPSC amplitude and inhibitory charge in PCs.
source: We determined there was a significant decrease in sIPSC frequency (Figure 2D) and a less severe decrease of sIPSC amplitude and inhibitory charge.
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2D showing quantification data.

claim: PC membrane potential and membrane resistivity were not significantly different between Control and Kit KO.
source: This reduced inhibition did not produce obvious impacts to spontaneous PC firing dynamics: we determined (in 29 Control vs 22 Kit KO cells) that PC membrane potential and membrane resistivity were not significantly different
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' electrophysiology experiments.

claim: Per cell average spontaneous action potential frequency, inter-spike interval (ISI), and ISI CV2 in PCs were not significantly different between Control and Kit KO.
source: we determined (in 29 Control vs 22 Kit KO cells) that PC membrane potential and membrane resistivity were not significantly different, and that per cell average: spontaneous action potential frequency, inter-spike interval (ISI), and ISI CV2 were not significantly different, despite some difference in the distribution of individual ISI across genotypes.(Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was some difference in the distribution of individual ISI across genotypes between Control and Kit KO PCs.
source: we determined (in 29 Control vs 22 Kit KO cells) that PC membrane potential and membrane resistivity were not significantly different, and that per cell average: spontaneous action potential frequency, inter-spike interval (ISI), and ISI CV2 were not significantly different, despite some difference in the distribution of individual ISI across genotypes.(Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The reduced sIPSC frequency in Kit KO was not associated with changes in the density or distribution of MLIs or in the thickness of the molecular layer.
source: Though circuit consequences of the Kit KO-mediated PC disinhibition were thus not immediately apparent, the reduced sIPSC frequency in Kit KO was not associated with changes in the density or distribution of MLIs or in the thickness of the molecular layer (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2 showing quantification data.

claim: Capacitance, input resistance, and spontaneous or evoked MLI action potential frequency was not different between Control and Kit KO.
source: However, capacitance, input resistance, and spontaneous or evoked MLI action potential frequency was not different between Control and Kit KO (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3B–E showing electrophysiology data.

claim: Direct electrode stimulation of the outer or inner molecular layer in a paired-pulse paradigm evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) of equivalent mean amplitude in PCs from Control and Kit KO conditions.
source: Direct electrode stimulation of the outer or inner molecular layer in a paired-pulse paradigm evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) of equivalent mean amplitude in PCs from Control and Kit KO conditions, and we detected no difference in the paired pulse ratio across genotypes (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3F–M showing electrophysiology data.

claim: There was no difference in the paired pulse ratio across genotypes between Control and Kit KO.
source: Direct electrode stimulation of the outer or inner molecular layer in a paired-pulse paradigm evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) of equivalent mean amplitude in PCs from Control and Kit KO conditions, and we detected no difference in the paired pulse ratio across genotypes (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3F–M showing electrophysiology data.

claim: Electrical stimulation can produce IPSCs of similar amplitude between Control and Kit KO conditions.
source: These data suggest that electrical stimulation can produce IPSCs of similar amplitude, and that release probability of individual synapses is unchanged, between Control and Kit KO conditions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their paired-pulse data.

claim: Release probability of individual synapses is unchanged between Control and Kit KO conditions.
source: These data suggest that electrical stimulation can produce IPSCs of similar amplitude, and that release probability of individual synapses is unchanged, between Control and Kit KO conditions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their paired-pulse data.

claim: The density and average size of GABAergic synapses onto PCs (triple-positive VGAT, gephyrin, and calbindin puncta in the molecular layer) was not reduced by Kit KO.
source: The density and average size of GABAergic synapses onto PCs (triple-positive VGAT, gephyrin, and calbindin puncta in the molecular layer) was not reduced by Kit KO (example immunofluorescence, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A; quantification, Figure 2—figure supplement 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, B, and C showing immunofluorescence and quantification data.

claim: Pinceau structures were preserved but smaller in Kit KO.
source: By parvalbumin immunoreactivity, these structures were preserved but smaller in Kit KO (arrowheads, Figure 2—figure supplement 4C)
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4C showing immunofluorescence data.

claim: Kv1.2 immunoreactivity in pinceaux decreased in Kit KO.
source: By parvalbumin immunoreactivity, these structures were preserved but smaller in Kit KO (arrowheads, Figure 2—figure supplement 4C), and this was confirmed by decreased Kv1.2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D)
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4D showing immunofluorescence data.

claim: PSD-95 immunoreactivity in pinceaux decreased in Kit KO.
source: By parvalbumin immunoreactivity, these structures were preserved but smaller in Kit KO (arrowheads, Figure 2—figure supplement 4C), and this was confirmed by decreased Kv1.2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D) and PSD-95 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4E showing immunofluorescence data.

claim: PSD-95 immunoreactivity faithfully follows multiple markers of pinceaux size.
source: As PSD-95 immunoreactivity faithfully follows multiple markers of pinceaux size (Zhou et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2020.

claim: Pinceaux size decreased by ~50% in Kit KO.
source: As PSD-95 immunoreactivity faithfully follows multiple markers of pinceaux size (Zhou et al., 2020), we quantified PSD-95 immunoreactive pinceau area and determined that pinceaux size decreased by ~50% in Kit KO (26 Control vs 43 Kit KO pinceau from n of 5 Control vs 8 Kit KO animals, Figure 2—figure supplement 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4F showing quantification data.

claim: Kit KO MLIs may have defects in physical and/or functional maturation of synapses onto PCs.
source: These results suggested that Kit KO MLIs may have defects in physical and/or functional maturation of synapses onto PCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their anatomical and electrophysiological data.

claim: In PCs of Kit KO, there was a significant ~50% reduction in the average frequency, but not amplitude, of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents (mIPSCs).
source: In PCs of Kit KO, there was a significant ~50% reduction in the average frequency, but not amplitude, of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents (mIPSCs) (Figure 2K).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2K showing quantification data.

claim: The average frequency and amplitude of miniature excitatory postsynaptic current (mEPSC) in PCs from Control and Kit KO did not differ.
source: In contrast, the average frequency and amplitude of miniature excitatory postsynaptic current (mEPSC) in PCs from Control and Kit KO did not differ (Figure 2L).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2L showing quantification data.

claim: Mean mIPSC frequency and amplitude in MLIs was unchanged between Control and Kit KO.
source: As MLIs synapse not just onto PCs, but also onto other MLIs, we evaluated mIPSCs in MLIs. Mean mIPSC frequency and amplitude in MLIs was unchanged between Control and Kit KO (Figure 2M).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2M showing quantification data.

claim: Embryonic MLI Kit KO was associated with a specific defect in the number or proportion of functional GABAergic synapses onto PCs.
source: Therefore, embryonic MLI Kit KO was associated with a specific defect in the number or proportion of functional GABAergic synapses onto PCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by the authors from their electrophysiology data showing selective reduction in mIPSC frequency in PCs but not in MLIs or mEPSCs in PCs.

claim: PC KL KO produced significant differences in the distribution of sIPSC event amplitudes.
source: Patch clamp of PCs in acute slices revealed that PC KL KO produced significant differences in the distribution of sIPSC event amplitudes (example traces, Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3B and C showing electrophysiology data.

claim: PC KL KO reduced the average sIPSC frequency and amplitude, as well as the total inhibitory charge transfer recorded in PCs.
source: PC KL KO reduced the average sIPSC frequency and amplitude, as well as the total inhibitory charge transfer ('charge') recorded in PCs (Figure 3D), without changes to PC capacitance or membrane resistance.
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3D showing quantification data.

claim: PC KL KO did not change PC capacitance or membrane resistance.
source: PC KL KO reduced the average sIPSC frequency and amplitude, as well as the total inhibitory charge transfer ('charge') recorded in PCs (Figure 3D), without changes to PC capacitance or membrane resistance.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' electrophysiology experiments.

claim: PC KL KO produced a substantial reduction in the frequency but not the amplitude of mIPSC events in PCs.
source: The phenotype was specific to GABAergic synapses: there was a substantial reduction in the frequency but not the amplitude of mIPSC events in PCs (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3E showing quantification data.

claim: PC KL KO did not decrease the per-animal average size or density of triple-positive VGAT/gephyrin/calbindin synaptic puncta in the molecular layer.
source: As with Kit KO, we detected no decrease in the per-animal average size or density of triple-positive VGAT/gephyrin/calbindin synaptic puncta in the molecular layer (n = 4 Control vs 4 KL KO animals, mean area 0.249 vs 0.286 µm2, p = 0.1962; mean density 0.045 vs 0.046 per µm2, p = 0.9658, not illustrated).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' immunohistochemistry experiments.

claim: PC KL KO did not produce a difference in PDS-95+ pinceau area.
source: We further detected no difference in PDS-95+ pinceau area (49 Control vs 48 KL KO pinceaux from n = 4 Control vs 4 KL KO animals, mean area 57.93 vs 53.37 µm2, p = 0.6036, not illustrated).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' immunohistochemistry experiments.

claim: Postnatal KL KO apparently reduced the proportion of functional, if not the absolute total number, of GABAergic synapse sites upon PCs.
source: Thus, as with embryonic Kit KO, postnatal KL KO apparently reduced the proportion of functional, if not the absolute total number, of GABAergic synapse sites upon PCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their electrophysiology and immunohistochemistry data.

claim: The frequency and amplitude of mEPSCs in KL KO PCs were not different vs Controls.
source: In contrast to this impact on GABAergic synapses, the frequency and amplitude of mEPSCs in KL KO PCs were not different vs Controls (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3F showing quantification data.

claim: A KS test revealed a significant difference in the individual mEPSC event amplitude distribution between Control and KL KO (p = 0.0002).
source: In data not shown, a KS test revealed a significant difference in the individual mEPSC event amplitude distribution (p = 0.0002, n = 1196 Control vs 1244 KL KO); however, the mean mEPSC amplitude was within 1% between conditions.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' statistical analysis.

claim: The mean mEPSC amplitude was within 1% between Control and KL KO conditions.
source: In data not shown, a KS test revealed a significant difference in the individual mEPSC event amplitude distribution (p = 0.0002, n = 1196 Control vs 1244 KL KO); however, the mean mEPSC amplitude was within 1% between conditions.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' statistical analysis.

claim: A KS test of mIPSC event amplitudes revealed that the mean mIPSC amplitude was ~10% greater in PC KL KO than in Control (p < 0.0001).
source: Similarly, a KS test of mIPSC event amplitudes revealed that the mean mIPSC amplitude was ~10% greater in PC KL KO than in Control (p < 0.0001, n = 5996 Control vs 3958 KL KO).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' statistical analysis.

claim: It is unlikely that decreased event amplitude contributed to the specific and robust > 50% decrease in mIPSC frequency detected in PC KL KO.
source: It is therefore unlikely that decreased event amplitude contributed to the specific and robust > 50% decrease in mIPSC frequency detected in PC KL KO.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their statistical analysis showing minimal changes in mIPSC amplitude.

claim: PC KL KO specifically reduced synaptic GABAergic inhibition of PCs.
source: Thus, as with MLI Kit KO, PC KL KO specifically reduced synaptic GABAergic inhibition of PCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by the authors from their electrophysiology data.

claim: Recombination by Pcp2-Cre begins at ~P7.
source: Recombination by Pcp2-Cre begins at ~P7 (Barski et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Barski et al., 2000.

claim: Pax2-Cre recombination occurs at ~E15.
source: Recombination by Pcp2-Cre begins at ~P7 (Barski et al., 2000), whereas Pax2-Cre recombination occurs at ~E15 (Ohyama and Groves, 2004; Maricich and Herrup, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ohyama and Groves, 2004; Maricich and Herrup, 1999.

claim: Continued expression of the KL-Kit dyad sustains inhibitory drive to PCs.
source: Our results thus suggest that continued expression of the KL-Kit dyad sustains inhibitory drive to PCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their comparison of embryonic Kit KO and postnatal KL KO results.

claim: Regardless of when KL was depleted (P7, P18, or P56), PC KL KO reduced PC sIPSC frequency and inhibitory charge transferred.
source: Patch-clamp recordings in areas of sparse infection revealed that regardless of when KL was depleted, PC KL KO reduced PC sIPSC frequency and inhibitory charge transferred (P7, P18, and P56 in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, H, and I; P18 injections Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, H, and I, and Figure 4B–D showing electrophysiology data.

claim: KL OX PCs had increased sIPSC frequency, amplitude, and inhibitory charge transferred compared to nearby Control PCs.
source: Whether at P18 (shown) or P56 (not shown), KL OX PCs had increased sIPSC frequency, amplitude, and inhibitory charge transferred compared to nearby Control PCs (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4F–H showing electrophysiology data.

claim: Control PCs from the PC KL KO paradigm received a similar degree of inhibition as did PCs from Sham injections.
source: We noted that Control PCs from the PC KL KO paradigm received a similar degree of inhibition (frequency, amplitude, charge) as did PCs from Sham injections.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the authors' electrophysiology experiments.

claim: While the KL OX PCs received elevated GABAergic input compared to their adjacent Control PCs, the (KL OX) relative local increase in inhibitory drive was not beyond the level of inhibition recorded in PCs from separate Sham animals.
source: In contrast, while the KL OX PCs received elevated GABAergic input compared to their adjacent Control PCs, the (KL OX) relative local increase in inhibitory drive was not beyond the level of inhibition recorded in PCs from separate Sham animals (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4F–H showing electrophysiology data.

claim: The local gain in synaptic input to KL OX PCs appears to come at the expense of decreasing inhibition to nearby Control PCs.
source: That is, the local gain in synaptic input to KL OX PCs appears to come at the expense of decreasing inhibition to nearby Control PCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their electrophysiology data showing that KL OX PCs have increased inhibition while adjacent Control PCs have decreased inhibition.

claim: MLI number, distribution, action potential firing, and the density of GABAergic synaptic puncta onto PCs are all apparently normal in MLI Kit KO.
source: MLI number, distribution, action potential firing, and the density of GABAergic synaptic puncta onto PCs are all apparently normal in MLI Kit KO.
evidence: This is a summary statement by the authors based on their data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 2, 3, and 4.

claim: While MLI axon terminals are present in Kit KO, they may be less functional.
source: These data suggest that while MLI axon terminals are present in Kit KO, they may be less functional.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors from their data showing normal synapse puncta density but reduced mIPSC frequency.

claim: An increased failure rate between action potential generation and neurotransmitter release would be consistent with the normal firing frequency and synapse puncta density but decreased sIPSC and mIPSC frequency observed in Kit KO.
source: An increased failure rate between action potential generation and neurotransmitter release would be consistent with the normal firing frequency and synapse puncta density but decreased sIPSC and mIPSC frequency observed.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation by the authors to explain their observations.

claim: Under the PPR paradigm, the apparently equivalent evoked responses may be due to direct stimulation of axon terminals and/or simultaneous recruitment of multiple MLIs.
source: Under the PPR paradigm, the apparently equivalent evoked responses may be due to direct stimulation of axon terminals and/or simultaneous recruitment of multiple MLIs.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation by the authors to explain their paired-pulse ratio data.

claim: Kit KO most directly impacts the MLI:PC synapse, based on seemingly normal miniature events for parallel fiber: PC synapses (mEPSC in PC) and MLI:MLI (mIPSC in MLI) synapses.
source: Kit KO most directly impacts the MLI:PC synapse, based on seemingly normal miniature events for parallel fiber: PC synapses (mEPSC in PC) and MLI:MLI (mIPSC in MLI) synapses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by the authors from their electrophysiology data showing selective effects on mIPSCs in PCs but not mEPSCs in PCs or mIPSCs in MLIs.

claim: Cerebellins impact multiple forms of synaptic input to PCs.
